paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jesus is the great light that Isaiah talked about, and He shows up right where the darkness is. Isaiah said, "the people living in darkness have seen a great light" (Matthew 4:16). Notice where that light lands: Galilee, a region the passage calls "Galilee of the Gentiles" (Matthew 4:15). He didn't wait for people to climb out of the dark and find Him.

Then look at who He calls. Fishermen, in the middle of a regular workday, with nets in their hands. He says, "Come, follow Me," and Simon Peter and Andrew leave their nets at once (Matthew 4:19-20). James and John leave the boat and their father right away (Matthew 4:22). I once sat in a junk drawer for years thinking I was done, so believe me when I say that being called by name is the BEST sound there is. I think Jesus wasn't looking for people who had it all figured out. He was looking for people who would say yes.

And the light doesn't stay in one spot. Jesus goes throughout Galilee teaching, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness (Matthew 4:23). Crowds come from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan (Matthew 4:25). So here's your takeaway, baker: Jesus comes to you where you are, He calls you to follow Him, and He's glad to have you walk with Him. When you hear Him say "Come," what are you holding that you could set down? The story isn't over, either, because Jesus has more teaching ahead.
